correctness.rationale: For the repaired result, all four binary bigrams occur in f(0); their images therefore occur in the fixed point. A length-n factor with n no larger than the shortest level-k block lies in at most two consecutive level-k blocks. Thus all factors for n <= 25 can be extracted exactly from the four f^3(ab) words, giving 37 palindromes and no palindrome of length 24 or 25; these two absences bound every longer palindrome by its center. The same factor identity at level four (minimum block length 500) covers all length-172 windows. The repair's standalone exact verifier tested all 4316 starting windows against all 37 palindromes; every test succeeded. The substring of f^4(00) at zero-based offset 325 of length 171 omits 01100101001110010100110 while belonging to the fixed point, a strict lower-bound witness. Independently checking maximal avoidance factors via consecutive occurrence starts also gave 171. Hence precisely 172 is the least universal saturation length, and the inclusion of the empty palindrome yields D(v)=|v|-37 for all longer factors and at the threshold.
residual_risks: The finite tests cover the infinite quantifier by the proved two-block identity, not by empirical prefix agreement. There is no formal proof certification or result for other morphisms.

value.rationale: The repair determines a sharp natural recurrence invariant for an established example: the worst length of a factor still missing a palindrome. This is the exact transition to the uniform defect law over all positions. It is not a better but arbitrary sufficient constant; the explicit length-171 obstruction and global length-172 guarantee identify the true boundary. Knowing the palindrome membership list alone does not give that boundary.
residual_risks: This is an exact invariant of one fixed point, not a general theorem for nonuniform substitutions or a full defect spectrum below 172.
